title: Your first agent: mini-dsh answers questions about files
brief: Build the first version of mini-dsh, a small TypeScript agent on Node 22 that answers questions about the files in a folder. It calls DeepSeek's Messages endpoint with fetch (no SDK), offers two tools, count_lines and list_files, and runs the agent loop with a step limit of 10. A tool that fails sends a tool error result instead of crashing. Every later module extends these same files (src/llm.ts, src/tools.ts, src/loop.ts), so keep the names from the lessons: callModel, textOf, tools, runTool, agent, MAX_STEPS. The tests never call the real API: test/fake-model.ts replaces globalThis.fetch with scripted replies and records each request your code sends, so you can check the whole loop without an API key.

starter.note: Node 22 project with tsx as the only dev dependency; run npm install once.
The Block, Message, Tool and Reply types are given. callModel, textOf and streamModel are stubs that throw 'not implemented'.
An empty tools array and a runTool stub. You write both schemas and both tools.
An agent function stub and MAX_STEPS = 10.
Reads the question from the command line and prints agent's answer. Complete; do not change.
Scripted stand-in for DeepSeek: queue replies (JSON or a server-sent event stream), then read back every request your code sent. Complete; do not change.
Checks the URL, the three headers, the body fields and reading the reply.
Feeds a stream split in awkward places and checks the text and the stop reason.
Checks both schemas and runTool against fixtures/, including bad arguments and an unknown tool.
Scripted turns: one tool call, two calls in one reply, a failing tool, and a model that never stops.
A 42-line text file in a docs folder, so the model must look for it.

hints: Build the request body once and check it against the lesson: model deepseek-flash, max_tokens, system, messages, and tools only when the list is not empty.
Push the model's reply into messages as an assistant message with its content list unchanged, thinking blocks included. The next request must carry the tool_use blocks that your results answer.
Put all tool results for one reply in a single user message, one tool_result block per tool_use block, each with tool_use_id set to the call's id.
Wrap only runTool in try/catch. A failed model request is not a tool failure and must still end the turn with an exception.
In streamModel, keep a text buffer and split it on a blank line (two newlines). A network piece can end in the middle of a message, and the stream test cuts it on purpose.

rubric.criterion: callModel sends POST to https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic/v1/messages with x-api-key from DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, anthropic-version 2023-06-01 and content-type application/json, and throws with the status on a non-OK reply.
The request carries the system prompt in the top-level system field, and messages holds only user and assistant messages.
Each request carries the whole conversation so far; the loop never sends only the newest message.
streamModel prints text as it arrives, handles a message split across network pieces, and returns the stop reason from message_delta.
count_lines and list_files each have a name, a description that says when to use it, and an input_schema with a required string path.
The loop finds every tool_use block in a reply, including two in one reply, and runs nothing the model did not ask for.
Each tool_result carries the tool_use_id of its call and goes in the user message after the assistant message that holds the call.
The loop ends when the stop reason is not tool_use, and stops after MAX_STEPS (10) model requests with a plain note.
A thrown tool, bad arguments or an unknown tool name becomes a tool_result with is_error true and text starting with Error:, and the turn goes on.
npx tsx src/main.ts answers a question about fixtures/ with a real API key, and the code keeps the lesson names (callModel, runTool, agent, MAX_STEPS).

milestones.title: One model API call
milestones.body: Write callModel and textOf in src/llm.ts. The test queues one JSON reply and checks the URL, the headers, the body (model, max_tokens, system, messages) and that textOf returns the reply text. It also checks that a 401 reply throws.

milestones.title: A streamed reply
milestones.body: Write streamModel. The test sends a server-sent event stream cut at awkward places and checks that onText receives "The capital" and " is Paris." and that the stop reason is end_turn.

milestones.title: Two tools
milestones.body: Write the count_lines and list_files schemas and runTool. The test checks the schemas, counts 42 lines in fixtures/docs/notes.txt, lists fixtures/docs, and expects throws for a missing path argument and an unknown tool name.

milestones.title: The loop with a step limit
milestones.body: Write agent in src/loop.ts. The test scripts a tool call followed by a text answer, then a reply with two tool calls, then a model that asks for a tool 12 times. It checks the call ids, the resent conversation, and that the loop stops after 10 requests.

milestones.title: Failures the model can read
milestones.body: Catch tool failures in the loop. The test scripts a call on a missing file and checks that the next request holds a tool_result with is_error true and the error text, and that the turn continues to the model's answer. Then run the agent once against the real API.
milestones.checkCmd: npx tsx test/loop.test.ts --only errors && npx tsx src/main.ts "How many lines are in notes.txt?"
